references.text: Jesus' first sign in Cana of Galilee, where he turned water into wine. John calls this the 'beginning of his signs' ([ref:Joh 2:11|John 2:11]), and in 4:54 the healing of the official's son is explicitly counted as the 'second sign' Jesus performed when he came from Judea to Galilee, showing that John intentionally counts the signs.

During the Passover festival in Jerusalem, Jesus performed signs that led many to believe ([ref:Joh 2:23|John 2:23]). These signs in Judea form the background for the second sign in Galilee and highlight the geographical movement from Judea to Galilee emphasized in 4:54.

The context of the second sign: Jesus went from Judea to Galilee ([ref:Joh 4:43-45|John 4:43-45]), and the Galileans welcomed him because they had seen what he did in Jerusalem. Verse 54 directly links the healing to this journey from Judea to Galilee.
The account itself of the second sign—the healing of the official's son in Capernaum while Jesus was in Cana ([ref:Joh 4:46-53|John 4:46-53]). Verse 54 serves as a concluding summary of this miracle.

John explains that Jesus performed many other signs not recorded, but those written are so that readers may believe ([ref:Joh 20:30-31|John 20:30-31]). The counting of the signs in 4:54 connects with this overarching purpose of the Gospel of John.
